{{short description|Theorem in mathematical statistics}}

The '''Kac–Bernstein theorem''' is one of the earliest and most well-known characterization theorems in [[mathematical statistics]]. It states that the independence of the sum and difference of two independent random variables characterizes the [[normal distribution]] (Gaussian distribution). The theorem was proved independently by the Polish-American mathematician [[Mark Kac]]<ref>M. Kac. On a characterization of the normal distribution. American J. Math. Vol. 61 (1939), pp. 726–728.</ref> and the Soviet mathematician [[Sergei Bernstein]]<ref>S. N. Bernstein. On a property which characterizes a Gaussian distribution. Proceedings of the Leningrad Polytechnic Institute, Vol. 217, No. 3 (1941), pp. 21–22.</ref>.

== Statement of the theorem ==
Let <math>\xi</math> and <math>\eta</math> be independent random variables. If <math>\xi+\eta</math> and <math>\xi-\eta</math> are independent, then <math>\xi</math> and <math>\eta</math> are normally distributed (Gaussian).

A generalization of the Kac–Bernstein theorem is the [[Darmois–Skitovich theorem]], in which the normal distribution is characterized by the independence of two linear forms of <math>n</math> independent random variables.

== Generalizations to locally compact Abelian groups ==

The first works devoted to generalizing the Kac–Bernstein theorem to locally compact Abelian groups are due to A. L. Rukhin<ref name=R>A. L. Rukhin. On a theorem of S. N. Bernshtein // Mathematical Notes of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR. — 1969. — Vol. 6. — P. 638–641.  https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01119683.</ref> and also to H. Heyer and Ch. Rall<ref name=HR>H. Heyer, Ch. Rall. Gaußsche Wahrscheinlichkeitsmaße auf Corwinschen Gruppen // Mathematische Zeitschrift. — 1972. — Vol. 128. — P. 343–361.  https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01111573.</ref>. These works studied the following problem. Let <math>X</math> be a [[Locally compact abelian group|locally compact Abelian group]], and let <math>\xi</math> and <math>\eta</math> be independent random variables taking values in <math>X</math> with distributions <math>\mu</math> and <math>\nu</math>. For which groups <math>X</math> does the independence of <math>\xi+\eta</math> and <math>\xi-\eta</math> imply that <math>\mu</math> and <math>\nu</math> are convolutions of 
[[Gaussian distribution on a locally compact Abelian group|Gaussian]] and idempotent distributions? Some sufficient conditions were established in <ref name=R/> and <ref name=HR/>. The final result was obtained by [[Gennadiy Feldman|G. M. Feldman]], who proved the following theorem.

'''Theorem'''<ref>G. M. Fel'dman. Bernstein Gaussian distributions on groups. Theory of Probability and Its Applications, Vol. 31, No. 1 (1987), pp. 40–49. https://doi.org/10.1137/1131003</ref>; see also <ref>G. Feldman. ''Characterization of Probability Distributions on Locally Compact Abelian Groups''. Mathematical Surveys and Monographs, vol. 273, American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 2023. ISBN 978-1-4704-7295-5.</ref>. Let <math>X</math> be a second countable  locally compact Abelian group. Let <math>\xi</math> and <math>\eta</math> be independent random variables taking values in <math>X</math> with distributions <math>\mu</math> and <math>\nu</math>. Then the independence of <math>\xi+\eta</math> and <math>\xi-\eta</math> implies that <math>\mu</math> and <math>\nu</math> are convolutions of Gaussian and idempotent distributions if and only if the connected component of the zero of the group <math>X</math> contains no elements of order 2.
